svg.title: Spring agentic workflow
svg.desc: Ten steps from ticket to merge in five lanes: the developer and the four gates, the main session, the six agents and the optional remote reviewers, the documents written, and what the plugin's hooks enforce. A fast path replaces the first three gates for small tickets. After the merge, a retro writes validated lessons into the project's knowledge base, which every agent reads on the next ticket.

text.tspan: From ticket to merge on a Java / Spring project. AI agents analyse, plan, implement and review; the developer decides at four gates,
the plugin’s hooks hold everyone to it, and every ticket teaches the project’s own knowledge base.
Small ticket: /approve fast — one page (02-fast-plan.md) stands for these three gates
changes requested: back to step 6, then 7 and 8 again
technical-reviewer — one lens per instance, in parallel
Code is locked until /approve go (or fast)
only docs/ can change, whether by Edit, Write or a shell command
until the last quality run is green and the code unchanged since
Approvals, the active ticket and its state are written only by the hooks, when the developer types /ticket or /approve — never by Claude
starts empty · grows with every ticket · committed with the code
read first by every agent, on the next ticket
Six agents, each with its own context and its own limits
+ optional remote reviewers: another model hosted elsewhere, reached over MCP (a Space, a team server, or your machine)
Maps the ticket to the code,
the ADRs and what the project
knows. Every claim cites a file.
can write: only the files its task owns
Proves each rule F1, F2… from
the contracts, not from the code.
can write: only its own test files
pass a gate — only you can
small ticket: one approval instead of three
where the ticket stands, what comes next
prepare a project · review outside a ticket
What stays true on every ticket
No code is written before you approve the plan.
Every business rule F1, F2… is traced to a test that proves it.
Test-first is your call, asked again on each ticket.
The functional documentation is updated before the human review.
Code leaves your machine only if you list a remote reviewer, and only the code the ticket changed.
